text:
maya: Quick sync — triaging private deploy scope for Q3. I put together swimlanes for low-touch vs enterprise on-prem customers and a short risk matrix. Want to land on a minimal launch slice by Friday.

sam: sharing the sketch now — low-touch = installer bundle + NAT relay fallback; enterprise = BGP/peering + IP preservation. Thoughts?

lee: +1 on the two lanes. Field has 4 customers who will only accept egress IP preservation and BGP, so enterprise lane is required. Low-touch should not block GA.

jamie: Customers asked for an explicit rollback window for upgrades (30m-2h depending on scale). Can we commit to an operator-backed revert?

sam: technically we can support a canary path and operator shim to toggle binaries; full stateful rollback is hard. Proposal: operator shim + image pinning + quick revert playbook.

maya: Risk matrix idea: (1) networking: IP preservation/BGP (high impact, field blockers), (2) installer: offline/airgap + KMS (compliance), (3) upgrades: rollback speed, (4) observability: tenant telemetry + audit logs. Each mapped to swimlane.

lee: For networking: option A = customer-managed BGP (enterprise), option B = relay/proxy with DNAT (low-touch). Need acceptance tests: preserve source IP, preserve ports, and deterministic failover.

sam: Implementation note: BGP requires docs + automation for ASNs and route prep. Timeline: spike (2w) -> automation (4w) -> field test (2w). Relay path is faster but adds latency.

maya: Launch criteria suggestion (must-haves): installer that supports basic NAT relay, documented enterprise handoff checklist for BGP/peering, upgrade playbook with revert steps, and E2E test harness for IP-preserve scenarios.

jamie: Also add a 'contract gating' item: any customer asking for IP purchase or long-lived peering must sign the network runbook. Keeps SRE scope clear.

lee: Edge case: customers behind carrier NAT who also want preserved egress IP — we need to surface that earlier. Could be a field exception.

sam: Quick config snippet we can ship in the shim (example):
```
# operator shim override example
image_pull: myrepo/redwood-operator:v1.2.3
networking:
  mode: relay
  preserve_egress: false
```
Not final, but useful for tests.

maya: Prioritization ask: we should backlog enterprise BGP automation but run low-touch relay path as GA fast lane. Who volunteers to own the BGP spike? @sam?

sam: I can take spike. Will outline acceptance criteria and a minimal automation plan by Wed.

jamie: I'll draft the field-facing runbook and signoff checklist. Aim to sync with Sam on Thursday.

lee: I'll collect the 4 field customer constraints and feedback, plus any NAT/carrier notes.

deploy-bot: deploy status: branch private-deploy/swimlanes pushed -> CI started :rocket:

maya: Okay next steps: Sam => spike & ACs by Wed; Jamie => runbook draft by Thu; Lee => customer constraints by Thu EOD. Maya to consolidate launch slice and publish PRD Friday.

sam: sounds good. If anyone thinks the enterprise lane needs to land earlier, flag now.

jamie: If field customers push hard we can cut a 1-customer pilot before GA. Keep that as an option. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks team — I'll create the PRD draft and add the swimlane diagram. Short thread, big impact.
